title: Polynomial-time proper learning of univariate Gaussian mixtures
decision_reason: Explicit source formulation, independently authored corroboration, twelve theorem-scope comparisons, current resolution/duplicate refresh and separated A60 self-review passed. Technical checks passed; no unresolved material status conflict located.

problem_fingerprint.objects: An unknown density f on R expressible as a mixture of at most k univariate Gaussians with arbitrary real means, strictly positive variances and nonnegative weights summing to one; k>=1 is an input parameter.
problem_fingerprint.access: Independent exact real-valued samples from f; k and error tolerance 0<epsilon<1 are supplied; no separation, bounded means, variance-ratio or positive-weight lower bound is supplied.
problem_fingerprint.output: An explicit list of at most k Gaussian means, strictly positive variances and nonnegative normalized weights defining a density g.
problem_fingerprint.target: A randomized algorithm and a fixed polynomial p, uniform in k and epsilon, with at most p(k,1/epsilon) samples and operations and probability at least 2/3 that TV(f,g)<=epsilon. TV=one half the integral of the absolute density difference.
problem_fingerprint.computation_model: The infinite-precision real-arithmetic sample model used by Daskalakis–Kamath (COLT 2014), Section 2, including exact Gaussian-density evaluation. This is an arithmetic-operation question, not a bit-complexity assertion for arbitrary real parameters.
problem_fingerprint.scope: Realizable density approximation only, not recovery of the hidden parameters or labels and not arbitrary-data likelihood optimization. The degree of the polynomial may not depend on k. Extra output components are not allowed; zero weights permit padding to exactly k.
problem_fingerprint.family_policy: One canonical proper Gaussian-mixture learning entry; do not count each component number, a metric convention, parameter recovery or a nearly-proper variant separately.

statement_sources.locator: Sections 1.1–1.3, pp.2–4: exact-k open question explicitly retained even without noise.
Section 2, internal p.5: explicit infinite-precision real-arithmetic model and total-variation normalization.
Section 1.6, author-manuscript pp.13–14, Open Problem 1.6.2 on parametric mixtures in the context of univariate Gaussian mixtures.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Proper semi-agnostic univariate learning with time (k log(1/epsilon))^{O(k^4)} plus nearly optimal sample processing.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: The realizable setting is included, but a degree depending on k fails the single fixed-polynomial target. The two-spherical-component multivariate result is a separate restriction.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Unrestricted means and variances, proper TV approximation and polynomial sample/time bounds for two univariate components.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: Matches the access and metric but fixes k=2. It supplies the explicit computation model and a partial case, not a uniform-k algorithm.

resolution_comparisons.source: LLM22 Theorems 1.1–1.3 and following open-question paragraph
resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Polynomial-k-and-accuracy robust approximation using O-tilde(k) components, and model selection with comparable slack.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: The output may exceed k by a polylogarithmic factor. No polynomial-time component reduction to exactly the target cap is supplied. The source conjectures hardness of proper learning even without noise; it does not prove that hardness.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Near-linear-time Hellinger density estimation with piecewise-polynomial output.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: TV^2<=2H^2 transfers statistical accuracy under the source normalization. It does not turn the output into at most k Gaussians. Efficient conversion would require precisely the missing proper-learning step.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Robust proper learning of arbitrary multivariate k-mixtures for fixed k, with poly_k accuracy dependence and k-dependent error exponent.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: Setting ambient dimension d=1 does not remove the k-dependent accuracy degree, constants and small-noise range. It does not establish a uniform polynomial in k and inverse target TV error.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Score-based learning under covariance, parameter-range and minimum-weight conditions; outputs a sampler with k/accuracy/conditioning-dependent complexity.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: The target requires an explicit at-most-k mixture for every univariate mixture without those restrictions. A good sampler is insufficient, and neither d=1 nor the theorem headline provides the missing representation guarantee.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Conditional density-learning hardness obtained from continuous LWE in a growing ambient dimension, with component count tied to that dimension.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: The candidate fixes d=1. This reduction does not imply hardness for that dimension. Projection onto an arbitrary known scalar direction need not preserve the distinguishing task.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Certified nonparametric maximum-likelihood computation for fixed-unit-variance location mixtures, with generic-data and accuracy conditions.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: The model fixes variance and optimizes over unrestricted mixing measures; the output support is not capped by the unknown true k. Wasserstein/parameter computation of the MLE does not give the stated realizable-TV learner.

resolution_comparisons.source: TD18 mog-sv specification, Theorem 1 and Lemma 2
resolution_comparisons.result_scope: NP-hard arbitrary-data empirical likelihood optimization for spherical Gaussians, including a two-component result and varying dimension.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: The data need not be iid from the target family, the objective is likelihood and the guarantee is optimization accuracy. It is not a theorem ruling out one-dimensional realizable proper TV learning.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Near-optimal robust statistical sample bounds via compression, with an exponential-time implementation and restricted computational lower bounds.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: Polynomial sample complexity alone does not prove polynomial runtime. A statistical-query barrier also does not rule out unrestricted randomized learners in the stated model.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Private parameter estimation using a reduction from nonprivate learning; the displayed polynomial-time guarantee fixes k and imposes statistical learnability.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: Unbounded means do not remove the minimum-weight/separation conditions or fixed-k quantifier. Private parameter recovery differs from unrestricted density approximation and is not a matching all-k theorem.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Proper sharp Hellinger estimation for fixed k, fixed-radius bounded means and unit covariance; explicit exhaustive-net runtime.
resolution_comparisons.assessment: The runtime exponent depends on k (the paper gives a crude n^58 example already at k=3). The source explicitly says it does not give polynomial runtime when k is an input, and its parameter restrictions are stronger than the target.

independently_authored_corroboration.assessment: Diakonikolas and Li–Schmidt are disjoint author sets. D16 poses the broader parametric-mixture question in a univariate-Gaussian context; LS17 explicitly states the Gaussian instance. LLM22 supplies a later explicit no-noise open-status discussion but shares an author with LS17. Versions and mirrors are not counted independently.

nearest_existing.difference: Existence of small encodings for finite binary concept classes, with no runtime requirement; no density model or Gaussian output cap.
A structural independence implication for Gaussian polynomial statistics, not density estimation from samples.
Prediction from labelled Boolean examples under the uniform distribution, with improper output permitted; distinct model and target.
Sample existence for private classification on finite binary classes, with unrestricted computation; no proper Gaussian density output.

duplicate_check.method: Established full inventory and metadata, fresh full-text searches for Gaussian mixture, mixture of Gaussian, proper learning and density estimation, and complete closest statements reread.
duplicate_check.result: No equivalent active or accepted draft. Authorized origin main equals local HEAD; connected GitHub search returns no open PRs.

normalization_checks: The density integrates to one; sigma_i>0 and w_i>=0 with sum one. Zero weights make at most k and padded exactly k equivalent.
TV is one half of L1; changing this fixed factor does not change polynomial learnability.
k is input, not a constant hidden in runtime; the same fixed polynomial bounds samples and arithmetic operations for every k and epsilon.
The explicit real-arithmetic model includes exact Gaussian PDF evaluation and does not assert arbitrary-real bit complexity.
No separation, parameter-range bound, variance-ratio bound or lower bound on nonzero weights is supplied.
The output need only approximate the density, not identify physical components or labels; empirical likelihood optimization is a different objective.
Success 2/3 is a conventional fixed confidence; D16 uses 9/10 and discusses amplification. Fixed-factor confidence changes do not introduce a distinct problem family.
All k, alternate metric normalizations and fixed-k special cases form one counted family.
